subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow persisted-session repair that removes only dead-end same-parent compaction siblings, or require write-side retry prevention before repairing existing forked transcripts?
rationale: The remaining fix touches persisted session history and may delete existing JSONL entries, so automation should not choose the permanent recovery policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept narrow repair policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental cache path, and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage.

options.title: Require write-side prevention first
options.body: Pause the load-time repair until compaction retry can avoid or supersede duplicate writes before deciding how to migrate existing forked files.

options.title: Reject deletion-based repair
options.body: Close or replace the linked PR with diagnostics-only detection if deleting persisted entries is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow repair policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR over current main, integrate the incremental cache path, and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is now a session-state policy decision more than a mechanical code routing issue, and current history points to Peter for the relevant area.
